sun-shower.context: A sun peeking out from behind a cloud with short rain streaks falling below. Used in forecasts for sunny spells with showers, and for fickle spring or summer days.

heavy-rain.context: A cloud with four long slanted rain streaks pouring beneath it. Used in forecasts and weather apps for downpours, heavy showers and flood risk.

rain-thunderstorm.context: A cloud with a lightning bolt in the middle and a rain streak on each side. Used in forecasts for thunderstorms with rain and for storm alerts.

snow-shower.context: A sun peeking out from behind a cloud with two small snowflakes falling below. Used for snow flurries between sunny spells in winter forecasts.

heavy-snow.context: A cloud with a dense field of snow dots falling beneath it in two rows. Used for heavy snowfall, blizzards and winter storm forecasts.

light-snow.context: A cloud with two small snowflakes spaced widely beneath it. Used for light snow and flurries in winter forecasts.

moon-rain.context: A crescent moon behind a cloud with rain streaks falling below. Used for rain at night in forecasts and weather apps.

moon-snow.context: A crescent moon behind a cloud with two small snowflakes falling below. Used for snow at night in forecasts and weather apps.

moon-thunderstorm.context: A crescent moon behind a cloud with a lightning bolt beneath it. Used for thunderstorms at night in forecasts and weather apps.

windy-cloud.context: A cloud with wind lines sweeping out beneath it and one line curling at its end. Used for windy and breezy forecasts.

snow-wind.context: A snowflake with curling wind lines blowing past it. Used for blowing snow, drifting snow and windy winter weather.

smoke-haze.context: A pale sun above three wavy plumes of smoke rising from the bottom edge. Used for wildfire smoke, haze and poor air quality alerts.

freezing-fog.context: Three bars of fog with a small snowflake above them. Used for freezing fog, ice fog and cold misty conditions in road and weather alerts.

black-ice.context: A road narrowing into the distance with a glossy patch on it and a small snowflake above. Used for icy road warnings and winter driving alerts.

rime-ice.context: A thin branch with a row of spiky ice needles growing along one side. Used for hoar frost, rime and frosty morning imagery.

dew-drops.context: A bending blade of grass with three round droplets hanging along it. Used for morning dew, moisture, condensation and fresh nature themes.

puddle.context: A flat puddle on the ground with a raindrop splashing into it. Used for wet weather, rain splashes and rainy day themes.

rain-on-window.context: A window pane with small drops and wavy rain trails running down the glass. Used for rainy day moods, cosy indoor themes and rain sounds.

snow-accumulation.context: A rounded mound of settled snow on the ground with flakes still falling above. Used for snow depth, snow cover and snowfall totals.

virga.context: A cloud with curved rain streaks that fade out in the air before reaching the ground. Used in cloud guides and dry climate weather for rain that evaporates.
keywords: rain that does not reach the ground

wall-cloud.context: A wide flat cloud with a lowered blocky step hanging beneath its middle above a ground line. Used in severe weather training for the wall cloud under a storm.

supercell.context: A tall storm cloud with a wide flat anvil top and curved bands around its rotating column. Used for supercell thunderstorms and severe weather outlooks.

microburst.context: A cloud with a downdraft shaft falling to the ground and spreading outward in curls. Used in aviation and severe weather for downbursts and sudden wind outflow.

noctilucent-cloud.context: A crescent moon over thin rippled cloud bands high above a horizon line. Used for noctilucent clouds, twilight skies and night sky observation.

altocumulus.context: Four small puffy clouds arranged in a regular grid. Used for altocumulus cloud patterns, mackerel skies and cloud identification charts.

nimbostratus.context: A thick flat cloud layer with a steady veil of rain lines falling beneath it. Used for steady rain, overcast grey skies and cloud identification.

fogbow.context: A broad arc drawn as short dashes above two horizontal bars of fog. Used for fogbows, white rainbows and atmospheric optics.

whiteout.context: A square view full of driving snow streaks with a faint walking figure in the middle. Used for whiteout and blizzard conditions with very low visibility.

dew-point.context: A thermometer with a water drop forming beside it. Used for dew point readings, humidity and condensation in weather data.

uv-index.context: A small sun with rays above three rising bars. Used for ultraviolet index readings, sunburn risk and sun safety advice.

pollen-count.context: A flower head on a stem with small pollen dots drifting off to the side. Used for pollen forecasts, hay fever and allergy alerts.

air-quality-index.context: A semicircle gauge in three graded segments with a needle at its hub pointing up. Used for air quality index readings and pollution levels.

precipitation-chance.context: An open umbrella with a small percent sign beside its handle. Used for the chance of rain in forecasts and weather apps.

wind-speed.context: Two wind lines of different length above a small speedometer arc with its needle. Used for wind speed readings in knots, mph or km/h.

wind-gust.context: Two sharp curling wind lines bursting in from the left with speed dashes. Used for wind gusts, squalls and strong wind warnings.

wind-direction.context: A compass circle with a north marker and a wind arrow with a feathered tail crossing it. Used for wind direction readings and wind vane displays.

wind-chill.context: A thermometer reading low with wavy wind lines blowing past it and a small snowflake. Used for wind chill and feels colder warnings.

heat-index.context: A thermometer reading high with a small sun and a water drop beside it. Used for heat index, humidex and muggy heat warnings.

feels-like-temperature.context: Side view of a head and neck next to a thermometer. Used for feels like temperature, apparent temperature and comfort readings.

air-pressure.context: A round dial with a needle and tick marks around its top edge. Used for barometric pressure readings, barometers and pressure trends.

daylight-hours.context: A half sun rising over a horizon line with a small clock face in the upper corner. Used for day length, hours of daylight and sunrise to sunset times.

temperature-high-low.context: A thermometer with an upward marker at the top and a downward marker at the bottom of its scale. Used for daily highest and lowest temperatures.

weather-forecast.context: A calendar page holding a sun partly hidden behind a cloud. Used for daily or dated weather forecasts.

weekly-forecast.context: A calendar page with a row of three small symbols for sun, cloud and rain. Used for week ahead and multi day forecasts.

hourly-forecast.context: A clock face with a small cloud overlapping its lower right edge. Used for hour by hour weather forecasts and timelines.

cold-front.context: A curved front line with solid triangles spaced along its upper side, the map symbol for a cold front. Used on weather maps and meteorology lessons.

warm-front.context: A curved front line with solid half circles spaced along its upper side, the map symbol for a warm front. Used on weather maps and meteorology lessons.

occluded-front.context: A curved front line with triangles and half circles alternating on the same side, the map symbol for an occluded front. Used on weather maps.

stationary-front.context: A front line with triangles on one side and half circles on the other, the map symbol for a stationary front. Used on weather maps and meteorology lessons.

high-pressure.context: A capital H centred inside an oval ring, the high pressure centre on a weather map. Used for anticyclones and settled fair weather.

low-pressure.context: A capital L centred inside an oval ring, the low pressure centre on a weather map. Used for cyclones, depressions and unsettled or stormy weather.

isobars.context: Two nested irregular closed contour lines like the pressure rings on a weather chart. Used for isobars, pressure contours and surface analysis charts.

weather-map.context: A folded map in three panels with a sun dot on one panel and a front line with a triangle on another. Used for forecast maps and weather charts.

wind-barb.context: A vertical shaft with a small station circle at the bottom and a pennant and feather at the top. Used for wind barbs on weather charts to show wind speed and direction.

beaufort-scale.context: Four rising steps with wind lines above the low steps. Used for the Beaufort wind force scale and ranking wind strength.

storm-warning-flag.context: A flagpole flying a square flag with a solid square in its centre. Used for storm and gale warning signals at coasts and harbours.

hurricane-warning-flags.context: A flagpole flying two stacked square flags, each with a solid square in its centre. Used for hurricane warning signals at coasts and ports.

barograph.context: A recording drum with a zigzag pressure trace and a pen arm beside it. Used for barographs, pressure recorders and classic weather instruments.

pyranometer.context: A glass dome on a flat round base with a stand, a sensor that measures solar radiation. Used for solar monitoring and weather station hardware.

weather-radar.context: A round radar dome on top of a lattice tower. Used for weather radar stations, Doppler radar and storm tracking.

radar-sweep.context: A round radar screen with a sweeping arm from the centre and two echo blips. Used for radar displays, scanning and live radar views.

weather-satellite.context: A satellite with two solar panel wings looking down toward a curve of the Earth. Used for satellite imagery, earth observation and forecasting data sources.

snow-gauge.context: A tall measuring stake with depth marks standing in a mound of snow. Used for snow depth measurement and snowfall reporting.

storm-glass.context: A sealed glass bottle with a long neck and feathery crystals growing inside. Used for storm glasses and old fashioned weather prediction.

weather-house.context: A small chalet with two doorways, a sun mark in one and a little umbrella in the other. Used for folk weather houses and quaint forecast toys.

weather-buoy.context: A floating buoy on wavy water with a mast carrying a small cup anemometer. Used for ocean weather buoys and offshore monitoring.

lightning-detector.context: A handheld box with an antenna on top and a small lightning bolt on its screen. Used for lightning detectors, storm sensors and strike alerts.

ceilometer.context: A small box instrument on the ground sending a dashed beam straight up to a cloud. Used for ceilometers, cloud base height and airport weather sensors.

four-seasons.context: A circle divided into four parts holding a flower, a sun, a leaf and a snowflake. Used for seasons, annual cycles and seasonal planning.

harvest-moon.context: A large full moon sitting low over a horizon beside a stalk of ripe wheat. Used for the harvest moon, autumn festivals and farming themes.

hibernation.context: A bear curled up asleep inside a cave opening with a small Z floating above it. Used for hibernation, winter sleep and animals resting through the cold months.

rainy-season.context: A calendar page with a cloud and a few rain streaks drawn on it. Used for rainy season, wet season and monsoon month planning.

daylight-saving-time.context: A clock face with a curved arrow looping around its left side and a sun dot in the corner. Used for daylight saving time and clock changes.

lap-timer.context: A stopwatch with a small flag on its face. Used for lap timing, split times and race timing.

wall-calendar.context: A calendar page hanging from a nail on two cords, with a grid of day dots. Used for monthly wall calendars and hanging planners.

lunar-calendar.context: A calendar page with a crescent moon where the date number would be. Used for lunar calendars, moon dates and lunar month planning.

advent-calendar.context: A grid of small doors in three rows with the middle door opened. Used for advent calendars, countdowns and daily surprise reveals.

leap-year.context: A calendar page showing the date 29, the extra day added in a leap year. Used for leap years, leap days and February 29 dates.

calendar-year.context: A calendar page holding twelve small dots in four columns and three rows, one for each month. Used for year views and annual planning.

monsoon.context: A rain cloud pouring over a palm tree whose fronds bend in the wind above a ground line. Used for monsoon weather, tropical storms and heavy seasonal rain.
